article.headline: Nucor Nears Its High As CEO Cites Strongest Steel Demand In 31 Years
article.deck: Nucor is 0.9% under a 280.21 cup buy point with a buy range to 294.22; the early entry at the 266.10 handle high is already 4.3% behind it.
body: Nucor makes steel and steel products. Its mills turn out hot-rolled, cold-rolled and galvanized sheet, plate, structural beams and piling, and bar steel, and it sells to service centers, fabricators and manufacturers. The business runs in three parts: steel mills, steel products and raw materials. It is the leader in the desk's metals group, ahead of Cleveland-Cliffs and Steel Dynamics.

The earnings explain the chart. September-quarter earnings rose 120.5% to 5.80 a share. Over the four quarters given, earnings climbed every quarter: 1.64, 3.23, 5.04 and 5.80 a share. Revenue rose 23.0% to 10.40 billion in the June quarter, up from 9.50 billion and 7.69 billion in the two quarters before. The payload carries no revenue for the September quarter.
The market is not paying much for that growth. Nucor is valued near 63.0 billion at a forward P/E of 12.88 and a trailing P/E of 17.68. The stock is up 70.2% this year and 85.4% over twelve months.

Nucor rose 3.78, or 1.4%, to 277.65 on Monday on volume 1.36x its 50-day average. It is building a 12-week cup, 18.2% deep, from an Aug. 5 high to an Oct. 1 low. The buy point is 280.21 and the buy range runs to 294.22; the close is 0.9% below the buy point. A handle high of 266.10 from Oct. 21 offered an earlier entry, and the stock now trades 4.3% above it.

The stock is 3.5% under its 52-week high of 287.70. It closed 9.1% above the 50-day line at 254.47, 23.7% above the 200-day line at 224.51 and 1.63 ATRs from the 21-day line at 262.00, so it is close to its buy point without being stretched. The RS line hit a new high, and the RS rank is 92 of 99 on the desk's list.

Headlines last week said the stock jumped 6% on a third-quarter revenue beat, with the company calling for a fourth quarter in line with or modestly higher, and that the chief executive said he is seeing the strongest steel demand in his 31 years at the company. Shares were at 278.99 after hours, up 0.5%.
The next report is listed for Jan. 25. Until then the chart question is simple: whether the stock can close above 280.21 in a market the desk rates in correction.

body: Tempus AI rose 6.26, or 8.7%, to 78.48 on volume 2.43x its 50-day average after reporting third-quarter results. Today's low touched the 50-day line, now 70.80, and the stock closed above it. It is building a five-week cup, 31.0% deep, from a Sept. 29 high to an Oct. 22 low, with a buy point of 89.19 and a buy range to 93.65. The close is 12.0% below the buy point. The cup formed after a bigger correction: the stock is still below its 104.32 high from Oct. 9, 2025, after a slide to 40.77 on July 28.

The bounce sets up an early entry above today's high of 83.52, with the 50-day line as the stop. The stock is 14.5% off its 52-week high of 91.83, 10.8% above the 50-day line and 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line at 71.70. The RS rank is 96 of 99 on the desk's list and the RS line is 20.8% below its high. Shares are up 32.9% this year and 66.8% over three months.
In the June quarter Tempus earned 0.03 a share after losses of 0.71 and 0.46 in earlier quarters, and revenue rose 21.6% to 382.5 million. The company is valued near 14.3 billion.

Headlines said Tempus beat third-quarter estimates and raised guidance as its oncology unit saw accelerating unit growth, and that revenue rose 23% while gains cut the net loss. Shares were down 1.2% after hours at 77.51.
A 31.0% cup is on the deep side, and the close is still 12.0% below the buy point.
article.watch: A move above today's 83.52 high, with the 50-day line at 70.80 underneath.

stories.angle: breakout past buy point, already extended

article.headline: Regeneron Climbs 3.6% As RBC Calls Third Quarter Strong Commercially
article.deck: Extended: 11.8% past an 859.44 cup buy point and above the 902.41 top of the buy range, 3.79 ATRs from the 21-day line.
body: Regeneron rose 33.37, or 3.6%, to 961.26 on volume 2.26x its 50-day average. The stock broke out on Oct. 30 from an eight-week cup, 16.0% deep, with a buy point of 859.44; that session traded 4.18x average volume. One session later the close is 11.8% above the buy point and past the 902.41 top of the buy range. The stock is extended, and the entry is gone until a new base or a pullback to a moving average.

The stretch shows on the moving averages. The stock is 17.4% above the 21-day line at 819.00, a reading of 3.79 ATRs from the 21-day line, and 20.8% above the 50-day line at 795.85. It is 1.3% under its 52-week high of 974.00 and up 30.7% in a month. The RS line hit a new high, and the RS rank is 94 of 99 on the desk's list.

The quarters are mixed. June-quarter earnings fell 4.5% to 12.23 a share while revenue rose 16.7% to 4.29 billion. The company is valued near 99.4 billion at a forward P/E of 13.72. The next report is listed for Jan. 28.

Monday's headlines said RBC Capital Markets called the third quarter strong commercially and a sign of core business health, and that pipeline progress and core brands drove outperformance. Regeneron also announced investor conference presentations.
A pullback toward the 21-day line, or a new base, would be the next place to look for an entry.
article.watch: The 52-week high at 974.00, and how far the stock falls back toward the 902.41 top of the range.

market_note: The S&P 500 fell 0.5% to 7,541.40 and the Nasdaq dropped 1.1% to 25,164.32, while the Dow rose 0.4% to 51,983.98. All three closed under their 50-day lines: the S&P 500 by 2.0%, the Nasdaq by 5.2% and the Dow by 0.4%. The S&P 500 carries 6 distribution days over the last 25 sessions and the Nasdaq and Dow 4 each, and the desk's read stays Market in correction. Energy leads the desk's groups with an average RS rank of 68, and five of the eight names still in a buy range are oil and gas stocks (ConocoPhillips, Cheniere, EOG, ExxonMobil, Chevron), though the four of them in today's stories fell 4.0% to 5.6%; AI infrastructure is the weakest group at 26, with 6% of its names above the 50-day line. After hours, Apple fell 4.4% to 323.42 and Palantir 4.0% to 171.20, both on today's earnings calendar, with Klarna off 4.2% and ON Semiconductor off 3.0%.

chief.verdict: Leadership has narrowed to oil, steel and drugs while the tech groups sit under their 50-day lines (only 12% of ai chips and 6% of ai infra are above it), and today the oil breakouts took real hits on heavy turnover: LNG fell 5.6% on 1.83 times average volume two days after its breakout, COP 4.7% on 1.41 times and XOM 4.0% on 1.21 times. When the newest breakouts in the strongest group get sold on volume in a correction, the risk leans down. The best setups left are bases that have not broken out yet, so the desk waits for the buy point instead of chasing.
chief.market: With the market in correction, 6 distribution days on the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 5.2% below its 50-day line, keep exposure light (no more than a starter position or two) and raise it only on a follow-through day.

picks.why: A 12-week cup 18.2% deep with the RS line already at a new high before the price, and the stock sits just 0.9% under the pivot after rising 1.4% on 1.36 times average volume. Earnings are not due until 2027-01-25, so nothing gets in the way of the breakout. The handle-high early entry at 266.1 is already behind it (the stock is 4.3% above it), so the trade now is the standard buy point. Risk: steel is a cyclical group, and a breakout in a correction fails more often than one in an uptrend.
picks.entry: 280.21, on a close above it with volume well above the 50-day average; buyable up to 294.22, stop 7-8% under the entry.

picks.why: The cleanest oil base left in the buy range: a 27-week cup 23.5% deep, the stock 1.8% over the 176.51 buy point, and earnings not until 2027-01-29. But today's 4.0% drop on 1.21 times average volume came on a breakout that only drew average volume (1.0 times), so it needs to show it can hold. Risk: a close back under 176.51 turns it into a failed breakout.
picks.entry: Buyable between 176.51 and 185.34 only if it holds 176.51 and turns up on rising volume; a close below 176.51 cancels it.

picks.why: The 30-week cup 25.7% deep broke out on 2026-10-29 on 2.47 times average volume, but two days later it fell 5.6% on 1.83 times average volume, which is selling in a fresh breakout. It is still 3.5% over the 300.99 buy point and inside the buy range, and earnings are already out, so the setup is not broken, only bruised. Risk: one more heavy down day takes it back into the base.
picks.entry: Only on a quiet pullback that holds 300.99 and a turn back up; buyable up to 316.04. A close under 300.99 is a pass.

picks.why: RS rank 96 and an 8.7% earnings jump on 2.43 times average volume off the 50-day line, but the cup is 31.0% deep and the stock is still 12.0% under the 89.19 buy point. The 50-day-bounce early entry at 83.52 puts the stop at the 50-day line near 70.8, roughly 15% away, which is too wide a risk to start a position. Risk: it gave back 1.2% after hours to 77.51, so the earnings buying may already be fading.
picks.entry: Not before 83.52 trades; better to let it build the right side and buy 89.19 on volume, buyable up to 93.65.

avoid.why: Extended 11.8% above the 859.44 buy point, past the 902.41 buy limit, 20.8% above the 50-day and 3.79 ATRs stretched, so a buyer today owns the first pullback.
Earnings land 2026-11-03, tomorrow, the last quarter's EPS was down 107.8%, and at 30.67 the stock is already at the edge of the 30.78 buy limit.

A valid 4-week flat base 12.8% deep, but it fell 4.7% on 1.41 times average volume and reports 2026-11-05 inside the next five sessions (EOG too, same date, after a 4.6% drop), so wait for the number.
The 5-week cup broke out on 0.65 times average volume, failed, and has now broken the 50-day line, 14.3% under the 22.38 buy point.

chief.watch: Whether NUE can close above 280.21 on strong volume while LNG, COP and XOM hold their buy points; if the oil names keep falling on heavy volume, the last leading group is cracking.
